article_identity.title: A Trace-Based Validation Protocol for Seed-Matched Evaluations of Black-Box Game-Playing Agents

decision_basis: Submission is prohibited while any factual contradiction, machine-verification failure, review criticism, human metadata/comprehension item, AI-completeness confirmation, ownership/redistribution decision, license, archive, or DOI blocker remains unresolved.

human_or_legal_blockers.required_resolution: The corresponding author must verify all 30 claim-ledger rows; no machine status substitutes for that sign-off.
Supply and approve every author name, order, and eligibility.
Supply and approve affiliations and complete postal addresses.
Supply and verify the corresponding-author name and email.
Supply ORCIDs or an explicit permitted none/decline decision.
Confirm CRediT roles for every eligible author.
Confirm funding and grant identifiers or approve a no-funding statement.
Collect and approve every author's financial and nonfinancial disclosure.
Approve acknowledgments and naming permissions or confirm none.
Every author must approve the final manuscript, disclosures, package, authorship, and overlap statements.
A human author must verify method assumptions, equations, signs, units, and interpretations.
The corresponding author must demonstrate comprehension of and sign off all 20 defense-guide items.
The human author must confirm the complete AI-use history and applicable privacy, access, IP, and tool-term compliance.
Identify rights holders and document redistribution authority for every proposed release component.
Rights holders must approve a specific license and its scope before public distribution.
Approve archive creators/version/maintainer/location and add a DOI only after a persistent record actually exists.
Confirm the exclusion list and permissions to identify organizations, packages, opponents, or people.

review_method: Three separate fail-closed passes were regenerated against the final Protocol Article: simulation methods, software testing, and APS general readership. Fixed status records whether the cited evidence currently resolves the criticism; it is not automatic acceptance of prose.

criticisms.exact_sentence: Schedule evidence can authorize only a matched-schedule description.
criticisms.proposed_fix: Keep the four evidence layers separate and prohibit stronger wording when a prerequisite is absent.
criticisms.reason: A recorded common seed is a design field, not evidence that executions repeat or that semantic random events are coupled across arms.
criticisms.required_evidence: An explicit implication map linking schedule, within-arm repetition, cross-arm event alignment, and statistical admission.

criticisms.exact_sentence: The timed-search interval resamples seed-condition clusters, retaining all four execution profiles together.
criticisms.proposed_fix: State the cluster as the analysis unit and resample all profiles together.
criticisms.reason: Four execution profiles reuse the same seed condition and are diagnostic views of one cluster, not independent observations.
criticisms.required_evidence: Cluster construction, 200 complete clusters, the 100,000-draw algorithm, frozen analysis seed, and an independent recomputation.

criticisms.exact_sentence: The restricted engine lacks these event identifiers, so its evaluations cannot establish this property.
criticisms.proposed_fix: Explicitly stop the restricted-engine claim below event alignment and reserve stronger language for the synthetic ontology.
criticisms.reason: Within-arm trace equality cannot establish cross-arm semantic event alignment after different policies branch.
criticisms.required_evidence: Stable event identifiers plus values, validated event-specific streams, or an event-keyed construction over a declared ontology.

criticisms.exact_sentence: This rejects exact repeatability for at least one exercised seed condition and identifies plausible clock or process mechanisms; it does not prove a unique cause.
criticisms.manuscript_location: Prospective validation results — Timed-search stress test
criticisms.proposed_fix: Report the observed divergence and candidate mechanisms while withholding unique-cause language.
criticisms.reason: Trace divergence under timed search is compatible with clock/process sensitivity but does not isolate wall-clock timing as the unique cause.
criticisms.required_evidence: A randomized or otherwise identifying intervention on the candidate mechanism would be needed for causal attribution.

criticisms.exact_sentence: Factorial acquisitions recorded schedule, boundary-seed, outcome, error, and decision-count fields; they did \emph{not} record trace digests.
criticisms.proposed_fix: Show trace evidence as unavailable and limit the admitted contrast to the prespecified seed-matched finite schedule.
criticisms.reason: Absent factorial trace data cannot be interpreted as zero trace mismatch or as a trace-parity pass.
criticisms.required_evidence: The frozen factorial record schema, processed factorial rows, and explicit admission decision showing bounded available-record evidence.

criticisms.exact_sentence: Repository history establishes that artifact ordering; it cannot independently prove when a human inspected uncommitted files.
criticisms.proposed_fix: State the repository-ordering fact and its epistemic limit without calling the work preregistered.
criticisms.reason: Commit ancestry establishes retained artifact ordering, not the unknowable time at which a person may have viewed uncommitted outputs.
criticisms.required_evidence: The protocol's first Git commit, descendant result commits, and a human account of any uncommitted inspection.

criticisms.exact_sentence: **Machine checks: PASS. Human verification: PENDING.**
criticisms.proposed_fix: Have the corresponding author review and sign every pending method/equation item; do not infer confirmation from passing tests.
criticisms.reason: Executable equation examples do not substitute for a human author confirming estimands, sign conventions, units, and scientific assumptions.
criticisms.required_evidence: A completed human_verified record for every equation and method, plus author comprehension of the analysis-unit distinctions.

review_passes.independent_assessment: The retained numerical and admission statements are simulation-methods consistent, but human verification of equations and assumptions remains open.
review_passes.review_scope: common random numbers, seed boundaries, event alignment, analysis units, resampling, uncertainty, and claim admission

criticisms.exact_sentence: Thus ``complete recorded trace projection'' always means complete only within this declared projection.
criticisms.proposed_fix: Scope completeness to the declared recorded projection everywhere.
criticisms.reason: Calling a digest a complete engine trace would conceal omitted raw observations, opaque search state, hidden simulator state, and event identifiers.
criticisms.required_evidence: A canonical serialization specification, explicit included fields, byte count, and an explicit omitted-state list.

criticisms.exact_sentence: Conversely, a digest is not a proof that omitted state agreed.
criticisms.proposed_fix: Keep the omitted-state caveat next to the digest claim.
criticisms.reason: Digest equality establishes equality of serialized bytes under the hash assumption; it does not validate fields that were never serialized.
criticisms.required_evidence: Trace schema, canonical serializer, digest and byte-count checks, and explicit scope limitations.

criticisms.exact_sentence: Checked tests validate the five fixed mode decisions, event-keyed repair, schema rules, and manifest-tamper rejection.
criticisms.proposed_fix: Retain the executable tests and make the complete reproduction report record their passing commands.
criticisms.reason: A software-testing claim requires executable fixture oracles and negative mutation checks, not only retained expected JSON.
criticisms.required_evidence: Tests for all five frozen mode decisions, event-keyed repair, schema rejection, and manifest tampering in an engine-independent clean copy.

criticisms.exact_sentence: The release manifest rejects engine binaries, model weights, archives, credentials, absolute local paths, and non-allow-listed files.
criticisms.proposed_fix: Fail release construction on every extra, missing, linked, stale, restricted, or malformed payload.
criticisms.reason: An allow-list claim is unsafe unless the built tree and manifest are checked for omissions, additions, restricted identifiers, paths, and prohibited payload types.
criticisms.required_evidence: A complete manifest, clean-stage allow-list, forbidden-pattern scan, and independent manifest verification.

criticisms.exact_sentence: Factorial records intentionally use \texttt{trace\_mode=none}; they contain schedule, outcome, error, and decision fields only.
criticisms.manuscript_location: Appendix — Trace record and study-specific fields
criticisms.proposed_fix: Keep factorial trace evidence unavailable and use only the frozen available-record gate.
criticisms.reason: A missing trace field must remain structurally unavailable; coercing it to a zero mismatch would create false evidence.
criticisms.required_evidence: Exact factorial schema checks, a table marker for unavailable trace evidence, and tests that reject unexpected trace-field claims.

criticisms.exact_sentence: Verification included artifact hashes, strict schemas, row-level reaggregation, independent equation tests, targeted software tests, comparison against primary literature, a one-command reproduction run, compilation, and page-image inspection.
criticisms.manuscript_location: Trace-based validation protocol — AI-assisted research methods
criticisms.proposed_fix: Run the one-command workflow after the last edit and bind its report to the final manuscript and release hashes.
criticisms.reason: The manuscript describes a completed end-to-end verification; that procedural claim must be backed by a current report from the final bytes.
criticisms.required_evidence: REPRODUCTION_REPORT.json with PASS, command results for hashes/schemas/statistics/macros/tables/figures/tests/contradiction audit/compilation, and final artifact hashes.

criticisms.exact_sentence: `MANIFEST.sha256` covers every staged payload except itself.
criticisms.proposed_fix: Retain the contradiction audit's manifest coverage and hash comparison.
criticisms.reason: A manifest claim is only meaningful if paths are canonical, every payload is covered once, and every digest verifies.
criticisms.required_evidence: An independent path-safe manifest parser and equality with the actual release file set.

review_passes.independent_assessment: Trace invariants, test scope, release integrity, and final reproduction are verified.
review_passes.review_scope: trace invariants, A/A and metamorphic positioning, schema/hash guarantees, tests, release sanitization, and executable reproduction

criticisms.exact_sentence: \title{A Trace-Based Validation Protocol for Seed-Matched Evaluations of Black-Box Game-Playing Agents}
criticisms.proposed_fix: Use the frozen title and article type in every identity-bearing file.
criticisms.reason: Submission materials for the wrong title or article category would misrepresent both scope and editorial expectations.
criticisms.required_evidence: Exact title and APS Open Science Protocol Article type in manuscript, cover letter, release metadata, and checklist.

criticisms.exact_sentence: Recording the same seed for two game-playing agents establishes a matched schedule, but it does not show that either execution repeats or that the agents receive equal random quantities for the same semantic events after their paths diverge.
criticisms.proposed_fix: Keep the opening problem statement, central evidence only, and one scope-limiting sentence.
criticisms.reason: A general reader needs the seed-versus-evidence problem before protocol machinery, a compact result summary, and a major limitation.
criticisms.required_evidence: A one-paragraph citation-free abstract under 500 words with supported central numbers and an explicit restricted-engine limitation.

criticisms.exact_sentence: The contribution is the operational integration of a declared recorded-trace projection, a self-contained conformance suite, and an executable admission map.
criticisms.proposed_fix: State the integration contribution and enumerate the established prior components without first/novel claims.
criticisms.reason: The paper must distinguish operational integration from prior CRN, streams, A/A, metamorphic, event-keyed, reproducibility, and work-budget methods.
criticisms.required_evidence: Verified primary literature, a sentence-level reference audit, and no unsupported priority language.

criticisms.exact_sentence: \author{[Author name requires human confirmation]}
criticisms.proposed_fix: Replace all front-matter placeholders only from author-supplied metadata.
criticisms.reason: A journal submission cannot contain an inferred or placeholder author identity, affiliation, address, or corresponding-author contact.
criticisms.required_evidence: Human-approved author names/order/eligibility, affiliations/postal addresses, email, ORCIDs, and final approval.

criticisms.exact_sentence: Public archival availability is not established: the author has not confirmed ownership, an open-source/software-data license, archive creators, maintainer contact, or a DOI.
criticisms.proposed_fix: Retain the explicit no-public-archive/no-license/no-DOI status until each legal and archival action is completed.
criticisms.reason: Calling a local review package public or citable without confirmed rights, a license, archival metadata, and an actual DOI would be legally and factually unsafe.
criticisms.required_evidence: Human-confirmed ownership and redistribution rights, an approved license, archive creators/version/location, and a verified DOI only after deposit.

criticisms.exact_sentence: The corresponding author must confirm the completeness of this disclosure and compliance with applicable tool terms, confidentiality, privacy, and intellectual-property obligations.
criticisms.proposed_fix: Complete and approve the disclosure without inventing an unavailable model snapshot.
criticisms.reason: The repository can record visible Codex use, but it cannot establish unrecorded earlier use or make the author's policy, privacy, access, and IP confirmations.
criticisms.required_evidence: Human review of every AI-use-log row, additions for any earlier substantive use, and author confirmation of compliance and final responsibility.

criticisms.exact_sentence: The practical recommendation is to identify exact artifacts and boundary seeds, audit row parity, repeat identical arms at trace-projection level across the contexts that matter, inspect stochastic sources, and suppress any claim whose required evidence is absent.
criticisms.proposed_fix: Keep the compact operational recommendation and the case study subordinate to the protocol.
criticisms.reason: The paper's significance should resolve into a usable rule rather than a list of game-specific implementation details.
criticisms.required_evidence: A conclusion that maps the four evidence levels to a concrete fail-closed workflow without repeating every headline number.

criticisms.exact_sentence: Suggested reviewers: **[names, affiliations, expertise, and email addresses require human input, if requested].**
criticisms.proposed_fix: Complete or remove submission-system-dependent reviewer placeholders under corresponding-author direction.
criticisms.reason: Suggested and excluded reviewer fields, if requested by the journal, must be selected by a knowledgeable human and cannot be inferred from repository data.
criticisms.required_evidence: Human-supplied reviewer names, affiliations, expertise, contacts, and conflict-aware exclusions, or an explicit none/not-requested decision.

criticisms.exact_sentence: Finally, author identities, affiliations, ORCIDs, CRediT roles, funding, conflicts, acknowledgments, complete historical AI-use confirmation, and permissions to identify organizations or individuals require human approval.
criticisms.proposed_fix: Leave the manuscript not ready until every human metadata item is supplied and approved.
criticisms.reason: These are mandatory submission, ethics, accountability, and naming decisions rather than scientific values an automated audit can fill.
criticisms.required_evidence: Completed human metadata checklist, author approval, competing-interest statement, funding/acknowledgment decisions, and naming permissions.

criticisms.exact_sentence: Verification included artifact hashes, strict schemas, row-level reaggregation, independent equation tests, targeted software tests, comparison against primary literature, a one-command reproduction run, compilation, and page-image inspection.
criticisms.proposed_fix: Compile, render every page, inspect it, and rerun the reproduction workflow after any correction.
criticisms.reason: The submitted PDF must be compiled from the final sources and every rendered page inspected for placeholders, clipping, tables, equations, signs, links, and stale artifacts.
criticisms.required_evidence: A PASS reproduction report bound to final hashes and a recorded all-page visual audit after the last source edit.

review_passes.independent_assessment: The article identity and scientific narrative are clear, but human metadata, rights, AI completeness, and author approval still bar submission.
review_passes.review_scope: scope, significance, readability, article identity, abstract, disclosure, availability, metadata, and submission readiness
